subject: Inference performance: p95 targets, concurrent streams, and MOP outline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@orbitalhealth.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medlytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-26T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Inference performance: p95 targets, concurrent streams, and MOP outline

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard, confirm success criteria, and propose next steps so we keep momentum.

Key pain points you shared:
- p95 latency is frequently spiking: current backend p95 ~350ms for single-turn generation (100-token prompts).
- Streaming UX: first-token delay and intermittent token burst jitter create a choppy experience in your clinical notes editor.
- Concurrency spikes: background inference bursts up to ~600 QPS during shift changes; current infra throttles and queuing causes timeouts.
- Cost sensitivity: target is to reduce inference cost by ~30% vs current spend without sacrificing output quality.

Current stack (as stated on call):
- On-prem/GCP hybrid: Triton endpoints + custom prefix/KV cache layer, running quantized LLaMA-65B variants.
- Request routing via an internal API gateway with limited autoscaling and no cross-region fallback.

Success criteria we agreed to validate in a pilot:
1) P95 single-turn latency <= 200ms for 100-token generations at nominal load.
2) Streaming first-token latency <= 120ms and sustained token throughput with <10% token jitter.
3) Stable tail behavior under 500 concurrent active users and graceful degradation up to 800 QPS.
4) End-to-end cost improvement >= 25% using batching/quantization/caching strategies while maintaining model quality thresholds.

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
- Naomi / Redwood: share a lightweight MOP (method of procedure) spreadsheet that lists sample traffic shapes, traces, and required telemetry (attached: mop_draft.xlsx).
- MedLytics: provide 24 hours of representative APM traces or a small perf dump (request files listed in the MOP).
- Redwood engineering (Rishi + Ben): evaluate a dedicated trial pool with KV prefix caching and a streaming-optimized runtime; propose a config targeting the above p95/first-token numbers.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (90 minutes) next week to walk your infra team through proposed proxy rules and fallback routing.
- Procurement: preliminary SOW and estimate to cover a two-week pilot.

Attachments: mop_draft.xlsx (MOP outline), latency_summary.pdf (short summary of the call's latency breakdown).

I'll coordinate internally and send proposed windows for the technical deep-dive. Please reply with any clarifications or if we missed something critical.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

--

Note: the MOP asks for sample request IDs and two sample prompts (one short, one long) so we can reproduce the streaming jitter locally.
From: Samir Shah <samir@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medlytics.com>, procurement@medlytics.com
Date: 2027-04-26T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference performance: p95 targets, concurrent streams, and MOP outline

Naomi — thanks for the clear summary. Couple quick clarifications from our side:

- The 350ms number is for single-turn requests routed through our API gateway after our auth layer. We observed additional 80–120ms variability when requests hit the affinity node that has the custom cache.
- Streaming issues are most visible when editors have live-collaborate enabled; average active token streams per editor during peak ~4.
- Procurement note: we'll need a pilot SOW that specifies a rollback plan and a data-handling appendix (we operate on PHI; redaction + KMS requirements apply).

For next steps:
- We'll extract a 24-hour performance trace and two anonymized sample prompt IDs by EOD tomorrow.
- Please include an SLA clause for fallback to a smaller model variant (if latency spike > 250ms for >30s) in the pilot SOW draft.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Orbital Health (MedLytics Subsidiary)
samir@orbitalhealth.com

Samir — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming the plan and a couple of tweaks based on your notes:

1) Pilot SOW: we'll include a rollback plan and a data-handling appendix noting KMS/HSM integration points. Ben will draft the pilot SOW and share by tomorrow noon PT.
2) Fallback rule: we'll propose an automatic fallback to a smaller, latency-optimized variant if observed p95 > 250ms for a sustained 30s window — Ben will itemize the compatible model variants and expected quality delta.
3) Telemetry: Rishi will list the exact trace fields we need (request_id, upstream latency, kernel time, kv_cache_hit, token_in, token_out). Please attach two anonymized request IDs when you send the 24-hour dump.
4) Technical deep-dive: proposed slots — Tue 2027-05-04 09:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2027-05-05 13:00–14:30 PT. Which works best for your infra and SRE folks?

- MOP draft (attached as mop_draft.xlsx).
